claims.text: Tailored severe thermo-mechanical processing can refine eutectic lamellar colonies into an ultrafine duplex microstructure.
Such refinement will simultaneously improve room-temperature tensile strength and ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a dual-phase lamellar microstructure.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 lamellar colonies are coarse.
Internal boundaries in the as-cast colonies are prone to initiate microcracks during room-temperature deformation.
Cold rolling followed by controlled partial annealing can refine lamellar spacing while preserving hard and soft phases.
The processing should avoid full recrystallization in order to maintain a microstructure containing both refined and retained coarse regions.
The two constituent phases must remain balanced during processing.
The treatment produces an ultrafine duplex microstructure that inherits or maintains lamellar features.
Microstructural refinement increases strength through Hall-Petch grain-boundary strengthening.
Well-distributed internal boundaries arrest microcracks and delay catastrophic crack propagation.
Microcrack arrest increases tensile ductility.
Relative to the conventionally cast baseline, treated material will have significantly higher yield strength and ultimate tensile strength at room temperature.
Relative to the conventionally cast baseline, treated material will have significantly greater elongation to failure at room temperature.
Conventionally cast eutectic high-entropy alloys exhibit limited ductility.
Conventionally cast eutectic high-entropy alloys exhibit limited ductility because of microcrack initiation and propagation.
Complete recrystallization would eliminate beneficial internal boundaries.
A processing window in cold-work level, annealing temperature, and annealing time is required to preserve lamellar integrity.
The optimum cold-rolling reduction, annealing temperature, and annealing duration are not yet determined.
The relative contributions of refinement and microcrack arrest may vary with strain rate.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis characterizes conventionally cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 as coarse and ductility-limited, whereas PMC4145285 describes the as-cast alloy as having a fine lamellar FCC/B2 microstructure with an unprecedented combination of high room-temperature tensile ductility and fracture strength.

Internal boundaries are initially characterized as microcrack-initiation sites but later as microcrack arresters. This could be reconciled by boundary scale or distribution, but the hypothesis does not clearly distinguish the harmful boundaries from the beneficial ones.
